items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: I played with Johnn Brown almost all of that summer... I left Johnnie Brown's band... I left Little Rock and went back to Johnn Brown, and played with Johnn Brown through '25, through '26 into '27

ctx.x: And so, I used to keep a diary of all these cities that we played, see. And I can remember in Corinth -- we played in Corinth, and that was where the Battle of Shiloh was fought on the Tennessee River. And I made a special trip out there to see where General Johnson was shot, and the tree where he died when they laid him up against a tree where he died. And that to me, that was American history, you know, that I wanted to see with my own eyes.

And I played with Johnn Brown almost all of that summer, until the latter part of August. I was offered a job by a gentleman named Gordon C. Harrison, who was a great pianist, and he lived in Texacana, Texas. They were opening a new hotel in Texacana called the Grimm Hotel, and this hotel

was built right on the state line. It was a brand new, beautiful hotel. And Gordon C. Harrison had heard about me, and they sent me a ticket. And I left Johnnie Brown's band, and I went to Texicana. I called my mother and them up and told them I'd be through Little Rock that evening, and they came over to the railroad station to say hi to me. And the train must have spent about 15 minutes there, and I passed through Little Rock going to Texicana.
